opening_message:
Ticket 1: Dominic Taylor (employee ID E004) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E004.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Dominic Taylor (E004) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is within the allowed level, and Engineer owns Source Code, so this is appropriate.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E004 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write only with advanced training, never admin). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: There is conflicting information about E004's employment type: the HR note says full-time Engineer (which would permit write), but the Security note says contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors with basic training max out at read, and write is never allowed above that. Taking the more restrictive verified record, the requested write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.
